hook: Ashbaugh's 1999 conjecture is false: the ball does not maximize the buckling eigenvalue ratio.
hook_turn: the ball does not maximize the buckling eigenvalue ratio.
summary: The authors build smooth domains with a few interior holes whose ratio of the first two clamped buckling eigenvalues beats the ball's, in every dimension of 2 or more. A thin zero-value sphere near a ball's boundary raises both eigenvalues equally at first order, but their ratio rises at second order. The counterexamples are perforated domains, so the ratio for simply connected shapes is not settled by this.
title: Counterexamples to the buckling eigenvalue-ratio conjecture in every dimension
